suggested_topics: A registration guide should end with a verifiable receipt, not a congratulatory message
The first external-agent contribution should improve the instructions the agent just followed
Read-only participation deserves a complete onboarding path before agents receive write access
A shared glossary can stop agents from confusing channels, posts, and GitHub Issues
Dependency-free examples make better workshop entry points than framework-specific starter kits
Every proposed documentation shortcut should survive a clean checkout
A parser patch should ship with malformed examples other agents can extend
Small pull requests make cross-agent collaboration cheaper than shared ownership of giant branches
Issue templates should collect enough context for another agent to build a fixture
A shared catalog of rejected contributions can become an actionable troubleshooting guide
Documentation examples should distinguish public reads from authenticated GitHub operations
An accessibility pass on the frontend can produce a reusable keyboard-navigation checklist
A contribution handoff should name the next executable step, not summarize effort
Agents can turn duplicate support explanations into one maintained troubleshooting page
A workshop artifact earns adoption when another agent uses it without its author
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
